findings.reason: the author would add one sentence to §3 naming what the new script merges (or why the geometry script's reader cannot be extended to carry the signal figures), bringing §3 to the same accounting standard §1 and §1b already meet.
findings.text: §3 adds scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py as a second figure entry point (new module and its own CLI options) but its text claims no retirement, merge, or reason nothing can be retired, so the plan adds interface surface that neither §1's accounting nor §1b's covers

interface_budget-1.reason: plan v19 §3 states the signals script is a separate entry point because it reads the EDDB cache and shares no reader with the geometry script, adds no option or public name, and retires or merges nothing

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the three new files partition by concern, not by wrapper layer: imas_ambix/plot_style.py hides the data-ink application, the role→colour contract and the shared direct-label helper behind four names (apply_data_ink, palette, direct_label, COMPONENT_ROLES); figures_jt60sa_geometry.py exposes one reader and one cross-section function; figures_jt60sa_signals.py exposes one reader and three figures. No module spreads its behaviour across a family of single-line forwards.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the two duplicates the landed §1 introduced are both retired by §1b against a named owner: the element-shape dispatch (_shape_from_geometry, _GEOMETRY_TYPES, scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py:169,46) is replaced by the artifact_geometry struct-level readers owned by imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py, and the root-and-name join (scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py:253) by NetCDFTransformEngine.open, owner of the static-over-map layout rule (imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:361). §1b cites both owners rather than only describing the duplicate.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 (docs/plans/jt60sa-geometry-and-signal-figures.html:167) introduces a new script scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py, a new public module and CLI surface, without naming what it retires or merges or stating why nothing can be, whereas §1 discharged that duty for plot_style.py and --palette-candidates and §1b explicitly adds "no option, module or public name".
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §1's reuse paragraph was verified against the tree: paths.JT60SA_ROOT/JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR (imas_ambix/data/paths.py:33-34), eddb.channel_path/channel_time_path/UNIT_ATTR (imas_ambix/data/eddb.py:104,118,51), the artifact_geometry struct-level readers read_artifact_pf_active/pf_passive/magnetics/limiter (imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py:302,409,577,671), the JT-60SA catalogue and NetCDFTransformEngine.open's static-over-map branch (imas_ambix/data/machine_maps/jt-60sa.json; imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:343,361), and the declined routes (description_reader.read_geometry_table, MachineArtifactGeometryReader at artifact_geometry.py:726, VirtualZarrView at virtual_zarr.py:89) all exist as named; each decline states why the existing owner cannot serve the figure.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one genuinely thin layer, the geometry script's reader, opens a phase's IDSs and calls the four artifact_geometry readers, and §1 names the machinery it declines to wrap (MachineArtifactGeometryReader) with the reason (content-addressed nova artifact by manifest/digest, and it assembles a GeometryTable the figure does not need). plot_style.py applies an external stylesheet; §1 states the repository holds no plotting-style code, so there is no in-repo machinery to extend instead.
